Name: hubness_penalty_metric_repair
Title: Mean-Direction Deflation Reranking: Deployment-Time Repair for Metric Misuse in Frozen Vector Search
Short Hypothesis: A rank-one mean-direction deflation reranker applied to the top-M candidates from a frozen inner-product index will substantially improve task-centric metrics on Iceberg's extreme metric-misuse regimes, recovering at least 25% of the performance gap to a Euclidean-distance ceiling -- and a coverage diagnostic can detect when reranking is impossible.
Related Work: Iceberg (Chen et al., 2025) exposes extreme metric misuse where IP retrieval yields Label Recall@100 < 1% despite Synthetic Recall ~100%. Centering Similarity (Suzuki et al., 2013) shows mean-centering reduces hubs. Test-Time DN (Zhou et al., 2023) applies mean-based normalization at inference. QB-Norm (Bogolin et al., 2021) and NNN (Chowdhury et al., 2024, EMNLP) use query/gallery banks for hubness reduction. Hubs in Space (Radovanovic et al., 2010) links hubness to proximity to the data mean. No prior work applies query-dependent mean-direction deflation to Iceberg's metric-misuse setting.

Code References.notes: Precomputed embeddings for ImageNet-EVA02 and BookCorpus

Experiment Plan.model: No LLM needed -- pure vector math with numpy and FAISS
notes: Training-free, no LLM needed at all
